subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap - PulseMed
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap - PulseMed

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps. Please tell me if I missed anything.

Summary of pain & goals
- Latency: current internal model infra has 250-400ms cold-starts and 120-160ms p99 for live inference; you need consistent sub-100ms p95 for triage scoring.
- Data isolation: must keep PHI in a controlled environment (HIPAA) — VPC + customer-managed keys preferred.
- Throughput & scaling: primary workload is real-time triage (bursty, 200-600 TPS at peak); want predictable reserved capacity but ability to autoscale for peaks.
- SLA: target 99.9+ uptime and predictable latency SLOs for the inference route.

Recommended Redwood Dedicated approach (high level)
- Initial reserved pool: 4 dedicated GPUs (customer-dedicated nodes) with autoscale burst to 8 during scheduled peaks.
- Isolation: VPC peering with private control plane and BYOK KMS support for keys; network egress controls.
- Performance: runtime config with continuous batching and prefix caching to hit sub-100ms p95 for the most common request shapes.
- Reliability: redundancy across two AZs; failover routing and canary rollouts.

Open items / questions for you
1) Procurement timeline & PO cadence (you mentioned Q3 budget — can you confirm target sign date?)
2) Any additional compliance docs needed up front (SOC2, BAAs — Marissa can help pull those)?
3) Do you have a hard requirement for on-prem or is VPC/private cloud sufficient?

Next steps
- I attached a draft SOW and the requirements matrix we captured on the call.
- We’ll do a technical deep-dive with Stephanie (SE) to validate throughput and test plan — proposed slots next Tue/Wed morning PT. Can you confirm availability?
- I’ll follow up with a cost estimate (4 vs 8 GPUs) and a draft procurement checklist for your finance/procurement team.

Thanks — I'll wait for your preferred times and any clarifications.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: PulseMed_Dedicated_Capacity_SOW_draft.pdf, PulseMed_requirements.xlsx

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pulsemed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: PulseMed Procurement <procurement@pulsemed.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap - PulseMed

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

On Jun 18, 2027, at 1:05 PM, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary of pain & goals
> - Latency: current internal model infra has 250-400ms cold-starts and 120-160ms p99 for live inference; you need consistent sub-100ms p95 for triage scoring.
> - Data isolation: must keep PHI in a controlled environment (HIPAA) — VPC + customer-managed keys preferred.

Quick responses inline:
- Isolation: VPC peering + BYOK sounds right. For higher assurance we may need a private enclave option — can you confirm whether Redwood supports dedicated physical isolation (single-tenant racks) or is the Dedicated product multi-tenant at the host level?
- Scaling: the 200-600 TPS peak is accurate; we also have nightly batch jobs that run heavy embedding workloads (not latency-sensitive) — curious if those should be on the same cluster or separated.
- SLA: 99.9 is our minimum; if you can offer 99.95 for the production inference route that would be preferred.

Procurement note: looping in finance (procurement@pulsemed.com). We target a signed commitment by end of Q3, but can accelerate if the estimate/contract looks clean.

Also: please send a cost delta for 4 vs 8 GPUs and an expected lead time to get dedicated pool provisioned.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Engineering Manager, ML Platforms
PulseMed

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, PulseMed Procurement <procurement@pulsemed.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap - PulseMed

Alex — thanks for the quick clarifications. Short answers below and next steps.

Isolation options
- Redwood Dedicated is single-tenant at the pool level: reserved GPU pools are isolated to your tenancy and we support physical isolation in select regions. VPC peering + BYOK KMS is standard; we can add extra host-level isolation if required (we'll flag that in the SOW).

Workload separation
- Nightly embedding batch jobs are cost-optimized candidates for a separate shared or lower-priority pool. That keeps the low-latency inference pool lean and simplifies autoscaling. We can include an optional batch pool in the proposal.

SLA & SLT
- We can target 99.95 uptime for the production inference route with standard incident SLAs and a latency SLO tied to the route (we'll include p95/p99 targets and credits in the contract).

Cost & provisioning
- Attached is a quick estimate: 4 GPUs (reserved) vs 8 GPUs (reserved + autoscale headroom) with monthly cost estimates and a run-rate unit cost per 1M tokens. Provisioning lead time: 4-6 weeks after contract + PO; accelerated provisioning possible for an onboarding fee.

Next steps
1) I'm attaching the cost estimate (PulseMed_estimate_4_vs_8.xlsx).
2) Marissa will start the security/compliance pack (SOC2, BAA) and coordinate any questionnaire responses.
3) Stephanie to run a technical deep-dive — proposed times: Tue 22 Jun 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 23 Jun 9:00-10:00 PT. Which works for your team?
4) I'll add a note for optional on-prem/extra isolation in the SOW and share an updated draft EOD Monday.

If procurement confirms target sign date we can prioritize the provisioning window in our capacity plan. Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachments: PulseMed_estimate_4_vs_8.xlsx
